q1_who.name: q1_who
q1_who.value: OVS S.p.A. is Italy's leading value/mass apparel retailer for men, women and children (also underwear, beauty, home decor), running a vertically integrated model across a portfolio of proprietary brands. Listed on Euronext Milan since 2015. Tier: MASS — live PDP price points observed €7–30. Channel mix: DTC-led via 2,600+ stores (primarily OVS, Upim, Goldenpoint banners) plus e-commerce and franchise/wholesale abroad. Standalone group (no parent); banners include PIOMBO, OVS Kids, Blukids, Stefanel, Les Copains, Shaka, CROFF. Markets: Italy core, with franchise expansion in Japan, Mexico and India.

q3_momentum.value: GROWING. FY2025 net sales €1,746M, up ~7% (≈3% organic + Goldenpoint acquisition), with adjusted EBITDA up ~20% to €218–219M. Momentum continued into FY2026: Q1 sales +0.6% to €354.4m, organic +7.5% YoY driving EBITDA +27% to €35.7m (9.4% margin); leverage improved to ~1.19x. q5_pdp.value: Measured live (24-SKU JSON-LD sample + 16-image vision classification on the women's t-shirt/top category): ~5.5 listed images per SKU. Image mix on the classified sample: ~56% on-model, ~38% still-life/packshot, plus occasional ghost-mannequin; 0% video. Shots per SKU vary meaningfully (2 to 7 images) — some SKUs carry full on-model + still sets, others are still-life only. Consistency = MEDIUM: backgrounds alternate between studio grey and plain white across SKUs, and shot count is uneven. Imagery is reused across marketplaces (e.g. Lyst carries OVS product shots). Net: solid, high-throughput catalog imagery with mixed on-model/still-life coverage but variable per-SKU depth and background consistency — the gap is throughput/uniformity, not baseline quality.

gap.name: gap
gap.value: THROUGHPUT and UNIFORMITY at studio scale — not baseline quality, and emphatically not cost. OVS runs Italy's largest, fastest-turning value catalog through an in-house studio that is effectively at capacity. The live audit proves the pain: on-model/still-life coverage is solid but per-SKU depth swings from 2 to 7 shots and backgrounds alternate between studio grey and plain white across SKUs (medium consistency). The single wedge is elastic AI on-model + still-life capacity that (a) absorbs new-arrival surges the in-house studio can't flex to, (b) standardizes shot-count and background across the OVS/Upim/Goldenpoint/PIOMBO banners, and (c) spins up marketplace and localized franchise-market variants at near-zero marginal cost. A 'cut your photo budget' framing misses — their in-house per-image cost is already low.

strategy.name: strategy
strategy.value: Scale-the-studio play, not replace-the-studio. Brand and group are aligned and both GROWING (FY2025 sales +7% to €1.75bn, EBITDA +20%), so this is a velocity/innovation pitch, not a turnaround or a cost-cutting wedge. Lead with the constraint: OVS ships more new SKUs per week than almost any Italian retailer and the in-house studio — not the budget — is the bottleneck on new-arrival velocity. Sartiq adds surge capacity that frees the studio to lead on craft, standardizes uniformity across banners, and unlocks the concrete localization lever: Japan/Mexico/India franchise imagery at near-zero marginal cost. Ride their existing digital/AI investment narrative (the €33m Puglia innovation hub) rather than proposing a visual overhaul — position Sartiq as the content-tooling layer that fits the transformation they're already funding.

Frame it as 'you're already investing in digital transformation via Puglia — here's the content layer that lets the studio keep up with your SKU velocity and go localized at zero marginal cost.'

input.name: q3_momentum
input.value: GROWING. FY2025 net sales €1,746M, up ~7% (≈3% organic + Goldenpoint acquisition), with adjusted EBITDA up ~20% to €218–219M. Momentum continued into FY2026: Q1 sales +0.6% to €354.4m, organic +7.5% YoY driving EBITDA +27% to €35.7m (9.4% margin); leverage improved to ~1.19x. Beauty doubling since 2021 (now ~8% of OVS sales), women's brands (Les Copains, PIOMBO) outperforming, and franchise expansion (Japan/Mexico/India). Brand and group are aligned (OVS is standalone) — no brand-vs-parent SPLIT. Management guides to further sales/EBITDA/cash growth.

input.name: q4_content_need
input.value: Inputs supplied to compute_opportunity (agent does not state €/image counts): new_skus_per_year=40,000 (tier-based estimate across banners); shots_per_sku=4.5 (live-measured ~5.5 listed images/SKU, ~94% AI-amenable on-model+still-life); channel_variants=3.0 (own site + marketplaces + localized franchise markets); refresh_factor=0.5; carryover_skus=25,000; revenue_eur=1,746,000,000 (confirmed FY2025); partner_multiplier=2.2 (multi-banner + franchise/wholesale); tier=mass. Model returned an annual image-volume range and € opportunity range with sanity check passed; the bottom-up sits above the top-down revenue cross-check, so treat the higher end as an upper bound. HUMAN REFRAME REQUIRED: OVS runs an in-house studio, so per-image cost is already low — the € figure overstates pure cost displacement; the real value is studio scale, new-arrival surge capacity and near-zero-cost localization.
input.assumption: SKU/year and channel-variant figures are tier-based estimates; shots/SKU measured live from a 24-product JSON-LD sample + 16-image classification. € is an upper-bound cost-displacement draft given in-house studio.

input.name: q5_pdp
input.value: Measured live (24-SKU JSON-LD sample + 16-image vision classification on the women's t-shirt/top category): ~5.5 listed images per SKU. Image mix on the classified sample: ~56% on-model, ~38% still-life/packshot, plus occasional ghost-mannequin; 0% video. Shots per SKU vary meaningfully (2 to 7 images) — some SKUs carry full on-model + still sets, others are still-life only. Consistency = MEDIUM: backgrounds alternate between studio grey and plain white across SKUs, and shot count is uneven. Imagery is reused across marketplaces (e.g. Lyst carries OVS product shots). Net: solid, high-throughput catalog imagery with mixed on-model/still-life coverage but variable per-SKU depth and background consistency — the gap is throughput/uniformity, not baseline quality.

input.name: gap
input.value: The gap is THROUGHPUT and UNIFORMITY, not baseline quality. OVS runs the largest, fastest-turning catalog of its peer set with an in-house studio effectively at capacity: live audit shows solid on-model/still-life imagery but uneven per-SKU depth (2–7 shots) and mixed grey/white backgrounds (medium consistency). The wedge is AI on-model + still-life to (1) absorb new-arrival surges, (2) standardize background/shot-count consistency across banners, and (3) generate marketplace and localized franchise-market variants at near-zero marginal cost. NOT a "cut your photo budget" pitch — their in-house per-image cost is already low, so cost-savings framing misses; lead with studio scale and velocity.

input.name: strategy
input.value: Innovation / scale play — brand and group are aligned and both GROWING, so lead with scale, not a turnaround. Hook: "Your studio is the bottleneck on new-arrival velocity, not the budget." Open with: OVS ships more new SKUs per week than almost anyone in Italian retail and the in-house studio is the constraint; Sartiq adds elastic on-model + still-life capacity that absorbs new-arrival surges and spins up marketplace/localized variants at ~zero marginal cost, freeing the studio to lead on craft. Ride their existing digital/AI investment narrative (Puglia hub) rather than proposing a visual overhaul. Route to Head of E-commerce/Digital + Studio lead; cold email default.
